title: Gemini Nano on device — Florina Muntenescu & Oli Gaymond, Google DeepMind
talk_summary: A Q&A-style session on Android's on-device Gemini Nano, accessed via ML Kit GenAI APIs and the AI Core system service, with a hybrid fallback to cloud inference via Firebase AI Logic. The transferable ideas are architectural: centralize a shared model behind a system service that schedules/queues requests, and route between local and cloud based on availability.

takeaways.technique: Hybrid local/cloud routing on capability availability
takeaways.what_they_do: They expose one API and route inference to the on-device model when available, otherwise fall back to cloud models, so the feature reaches all devices without per-device work.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if we have Gemini Nano available on device then you can run that inference on device. Otherwise it can run on the cloud

takeaways.technique: Centralized model service with request queuing and priority
takeaways.what_they_do: A single system service owns the model, queues requests from all consumers, and prioritizes foreground/active work over background work.
takeaways.numbers: model ~3-4 GB shared across all apps

takeaways.technique: Share one expensive resource across many consumers
takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of each app shipping its own model, the OS ships one model once and all apps share it, centralizing the cost.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If we put this in the system, we do that once and everyone can share and benefit from it, well, that shares that cost
takeaways.numbers: smallest useful models ~1 GB; shipped ~3-4 GB

takeaways.technique: Offload heavy/batch work to idle capacity
takeaways.what_they_do: Latency-insensitive batch jobs are run in the background, e.g. overnight while charging, rather than competing with interactive use.
takeaways.evidence_quote: often times that's not necessarily latency sensitive so people are using that in the background perhaps when it's running overcharge overnight
